text.p: Shareholders of Polish paintmaker Polifarb Wroclaw approved a merger with Polifarb Cieszyn but did not vote on Cieszyn's Monday decision to acquire 53.5 percent of the new firm, a Wroclaw official said.

Deputy president of Polifarb Wroclaw Wojciech Solarski said on Tuesday the company's extraordinary shareholders meeting voted for all the necessary motions to carry out the merger including the one-for-one share exchange to effect it.
"All the necessary motions to carry out a merger with Polifarb Cieszyn were passed, we will have the merger," he said.

Solarski said Wroclaw shareholders did not vote on the Cieszyn shareholders decision that after the merger they should have 53.5 percent in the merged firm and current Wroclaw shareholders 46.5 percent.

On Monday Cieszyn shareholders voted to increase a bonus issue to 6.375 million shares from the earlier planned 2.98 million shares before the merger, to give them later the 53.5 percent control in the new firm.
"The merger will go ahead no matter what will be with the bonus issue," he said.
Solarski also said the Cieszyn's motion on the scrip issue could yet be challenged, after one of Cieszyn's shareholders Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych (BIG) said it was illegal.
"Yesterday BIG protested against the motion and it can yet be disputed and taken to commercial court," he said.
BIG, which has six percent of Cieszyn through its subsidiaries, declined comment on the issue.

Originally, both companies were to hold 50 percent each in the merged firm, Polifarb Cieszyn-Wroclaw SA, which would command 26 percent of the Polish paint market and account for 40 percent of domestic paint production.
